title: Wyandance / Wyandanch
summary: Wyandance, now Wyandanch, is a Babylon placename preserving the name of the seventeenth-century sachem of Paumanack.
introduction_content: Wyandance names the locality formerly known as West Deer Park in the town of Babylon. The name is also written Waiandance and Wayan-taunche, and survives today as Wyandanch.
history_content: The locality name commemorates Wyandanch, a sachem of Paumanack whose authority and diplomacy shaped seventeenth-century Long Island history. The modern map point marks the Babylon hamlet, not Wyandanch's Montauk village.
translation_content:
The name is interpreted as "the wise speaker or talker," connected with terms for wisdom and speaking.

Why Place Names Matter

“The keys to these stories are often the names for places or the names of ancestors whose deeds or experiences are linked to the location.”

— Andrew M. Miller, Barry Ahenakew: Place Names of the nêhiyawak (2021), Cree Literacy Network project introduction
preservation_content: The history separates the modern placename from the broader life and homelands of Wyandanch while preserving the historic naming record and its later official use.
whereintheworld_content: Approximate blue/general placement in modern Wyandanch, Town of Babylon. Coordinates mark the hamlet and are not a historic residence or village location.
